name: PIR motion sensor
description: Passive-infrared motion sensor module (HC-SR501, BISS0001): about a minute's warm-up after power-up; motion raises OUT (3.3 V) for the hold time Tx; with the jumper at H (default) motion during Tx restarts it, at L OUT falls Tx after it rose; after OUT falls the controller blocks for about 2.5 s. Motion is an interactive input or, left unset, a warm body (a person, an animal) moving within the lens's 110-degree field of view and its 3 to 7 m range.

hold.doc: Tx: how long OUT stays high (the 'time' trimmer, about 3 s to 300 s on the module)

warmup.doc: Initialisation after power-up, OUT low and motion unseen (about a minute per the datasheet)

lockout.doc: Ti: the BISS0001's block after OUT falls (about 2.5 s on the module)

retrigger.doc: Jumper at H (repeatable trigger) rather than L (single trigger)

fov.doc: The Fresnel lens's field of view (cone angle) for the world's bodies

range.doc: How far a warm body is seen (the sensitivity trimmer, about 3 to 7 m)

zone.doc: The width of the Fresnel lens's view cones, across and up: the element sees a warm body change cones (walking across is seen sooner than walking straight at it); 0 for no lens. The HC-SR501's lens pitch is not published: 7.5 deg is an assumption

inputs.name: motion
inputs.doc: Something warm moves in front of the sensor; left unset, read from the world (a warm body moving in the field of view)

functional.claims: Warm-up, hold time Tx, H (retrigger) and L (single) modes, the ~2.5 s block after OUT falls; motion from the world as a warm body whose image crosses from one of the Fresnel lens's view cones to the next (or into or out of view) within the field of view and range, looked at every 100 ms, so walking across is seen sooner than walking straight at it. The world's motion is checked end to end by tests/protocol/test_pir.py.
omissions: the lens's real pattern (its cones are a regular grid zone_deg wide, the HC-SR501's pitch being unpublished), the element's response to a body's speed and size (any cone crossed counts, however fast or slow)
the temperature difference needed (a body is warm or not)
output glitches during warm-up (0 to 3 toggles on the module)
